title: observability: token-level cost/latency metrics, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Provide token-level cost and latency visibility end-to-end and make alert thresholds actionable for SRE/Platform. This PR adds new Prometheus metrics that attribute USD cost per token, enriches tracing with token-level span tags, ships a Grafana dashboard for token cost/latency breakdowns, and updates alert rules and runbooks. Scope: 1) metrics: add counter gauges and histograms exposed by the serving runtime and batching layer; 2) tracing: add token_count and token_cost_usd tags to request spans and batch spans; 3) dashboards: new Grafana dashboard with per-model and per-route panels, cost heatmaps, p50/p95/p99 token latencies, and token-cost-per-token distributions; 4) alert tuning: new firing rules and thresholds, plus a short runbook in docs. Checklist: - [x] Add Prometheus metrics and instrumentation in runtime (- redwood/observability/metrics/token_cost_metrics.go) - [x] Add span tags in tracing pipeline (- redwood/observability/tracing/span_tags.go) - [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON and reference link (- infra/grafana/dashboards/token_cost_latency.json) - [x] Add Prometheus alerting rules and link to runbook (- infra/alerts/token_latency.rules.yml, docs/observability/token-level-metrics.md) - [x] Unit and integration tests for metric emission (- tests/observability/metrics_test.go) - [x] Load test validation on staging for metric cardinality and scrape performance (staging run 2026-02-18) Implementation notes: - New metrics introduced: redwood_token_cost_usd_total (counter, labels: model, route, customer_id, hardware_class), redwood_token_processing_seconds_bucket (histogram, labels: model, route), redwood_token_count_total (counter). - Metrics are emitted at the batching layer after KV-cache and after suffix generation to avoid double-counting. - Tracing: spans now include tags token_count and token_cost_usd. We limit token_count cardinality by sampling on high-card routes and adding a max_tokens_bucket label (<=16, <=64, <=256, >256). - Dashboard: uses derived Prometheus queries to compute cost-per-1k-tokens and cost-per-request. Panels include configurable time-range breakdowns and a heatmap for cost spikes. - Alert rules: tuned alerts for sustained p95 token latency > 120ms, token-cost growth > 3x week-over-week for a customer, and scrape error rate > 2% sustained. Runbook: attached doc includes triage steps, cost mitigation (pin model, enable caching, enable quantization profile), and on-call contacts. Backwards compatibility: metrics are additive and namespaced under redwood_; default labels are optional; feature guarded behind runtime flag "enable_token_level_metrics" (defaults to false for existing clusters). Performance impact: staging load test reported 3.4% increase in scrape payload size at 1M requests/day and <1% CPU overhead on the runtime in typical traffic profiles. Follow-ups: - add a prometheus relabeling config to drop high-card customer_id in long-term retention clusters (ENG-3360) - add SDK helpers to surface cost-per-call in usage API (ENG-3361) Example snippet (instrumentation): "// emit token cost metric
redwood_token_cost_usd_total.WithLabelValues(model, route, customerID, hwClass).Add(costUsd)
// add span tags
span.SetTag("token_count", tokenCount)
span.SetTag("token_cost_usd", fmt.Sprintf("%.6f", costUsd))"

release_notes: Added token-level cost and latency observability: new Prometheus metrics (redwood_token_cost_usd_total, redwood_token_processing_seconds), tracing tags (token_count, token_cost_usd), Grafana dashboard for token cost/latency, and tuned alerting rules + runbook. Feature gated behind enable_token_level_metrics flag; opt-in required for production clusters.
notes: Deployed to staging 2026-02-18, monitored for 48 hours. Metrics cardinality within expected bounds after relabeling; no customer-facing changes. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-3360 and ENG-3361.
risk_assessment: Low-medium; additive metrics and behind feature flag. Main risk is high-cardinality labels — mitigated via sampling, max_tokens_bucket label, and relabeling in long-term retention clusters.
